calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Kings are one of the league’s best for shot volume, and the Avalanche are one of the league’s best at keeping shots away. We think the Kings still get theirs.
calls.call: The Kings take more than the league-average 56.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 against the Avalanche.
calls.nums: Los Angeles 4th for shot volume (60.8 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Colorado 5th for keeping shots away
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts, Los Angeles had 56.6 per 60. The league average is 56.3 per 60, and they came in at 60.8 per 60.

calls.head: The Avalanche’s defense joins the attack; the Kings’ stays home
calls.body: The Avalanche are one of the league’s best for shots from defensemen, at the active D end; the Kings are the league’s worst, at the forward-led end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Avalanche’s defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Kings’.
calls.nums: Shots from defensemen: Colorado 2nd, Los Angeles 32nd
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On share of 5-on-5 shot attempts taken by defensemen, Colorado had 25% and Los Angeles 33%. Coming in, Colorado was at 40% and Los Angeles at 30%.

COL.head: We gave Colorado a 64% chance, and Colorado delivered.

LAK.head: We gave Los Angeles only a 36% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: A rough night for D. Kuemper
surprises.body: D. Kuemper allowed 8 goals on shots worth 3.5 expected goals, 4.5 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 350 starts over the last three seasons.

story.head: The Avalanche roll past the Kings
paras: Brock Nelson opened the scoring early in the first. Nathan MacKinnon and Artturi Lehkonen added two each. Six different Avalanche scored.
The chances were closer than the score. By our Swing measure, Nicolas Roy had the best night of anyone.

items.text: One of the preview’s two calls held.
